previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after noticing blood in her nephrostomy tube one week following coil embolization of a failed kidney transplant. She had no pain or fever but presented with an elevated white blood cell count. Imaging showed expected post-embolization changes with scattered echogenic foci suggestive of gas. A sample from the tube grew VRE, but blood cultures were negative and her WBC improved with a single dose of vancomycin. The nephrostomy tube was removed without complication, and she remained stable. Warfarin was restarted, midodrine was added for dialysis-related hypotension, and she completed a short prednisone taper. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue outpatient hemodialysis, monitor the drain site, and follow up with her nephrologist.

#E COLI BACTEREMIA/SEPSIS: Pt was initially treated empirically 
with linezolid, cefepime, and metronidazole. Blood cultures 
eventually returned positive for E. coli. On ___ the three 
antibiotics were stopped and she was switched to iv ceftazidime 
2g to be given on HD days (___). 
Subsequent blood cultures remained negative. Early in her stay 
she spiked fevers daily but after she was transferred to ___ 
campus she remained afebrile without complaint. Source of E coli 
is not quite clear; possible sources include:

1. Biliary tract: abd CT on admission notable for dilated common 
bile duct. For this reason, patient was admitted to the ___ 
campus for possible ERCP. However, she had no abdominal pain, 
and normal LFTs, so cholecystitis/cholangitis was thought 
unlikely. Nonetheless, endoscopic ultrasound was done on ___ 
which showed cholelithiasis but no obstruction or sludge. It is 
possible that she devloped bacteremia from transient 
obstruction.

CT findings.

Specimen (only 1cc) was obtained on the floor by straight cath 
the following day. Culture was negative, but she had already 
received antibiotics. 

4. Cyst infection: ID was consulted on ___ re: persistent fever 
in an immunosuppressed patient and for help identifying the 
source of E coli.  They felt that the pt may have an infected 
cyst, which they have seen in other pts with PCKD.  These 
infections are usually hard to find and respond to prolonged 
courses of antibiotics.  Therefore, a tagged WBC scan was 
performed on ___ to ___ which did not reveal a nidus of 
infection.  ID recommended three weeks of IV ceftazidime, to be 
given at HD sessinos.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ woman with polycystic kidney disease status post failed
renal transplant, on hemodialysis, admitted with fevers.  CT scan showed
possible common bile duct dilatation, please perform without contrast as the
patient is on dialysis.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted images were acquired on a 1.5
Tesla magnet.  Intravenous contrast was not administered as the patient has
end-stage renal failure.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis ___ and MR abdomen and pelvis
___.

FINDINGS:  There are innumerable hepatic cysts.  The largest is a
heterogeneously T2-hypointense lesion in segment VII/VIII measuring 6.6 x 6.6
cm.  This is heterogeneously hyperintense on non-contrast T1-weighted images
consistent with blood degradation products.  Evaluation of the liver is
limited by the lack of intravenous contrast; however, no concerning lesions
are identified.  

There is mild intrahepatic duct dilatation.  The common bile duct measures 1.3
cm and tapers relatively abruptly at the level of the ampulla.  The common
bile duct has a very similar appearance in ___, when it measured 1 cm.  The
appearances could be due to an ampullary stenosis; however, given the slow
interval progression, this is unlikely to be clinically significant.  

Gallstones noted within the gallbladder.  There is heterogeneous thickening
and cystic appearance of the gallbladder fundus consistent with
adenomyomatosis. 

There is a small amount of free fluid around the liver, likely related to the
patient's renal failure.  The pancreas is normal in signal intensity and
morphology; however, there is a 1.9-cm cyst in the pancreatic body which was
not apparent on the prior study in ___.  No internal septations are seen and
this cyst is remote from the pancreatic duct. The pancreatic duct is not
dilated.  The spleen is moderately enlarged measuring 15 cm.  There is a
heterogeneously T2-hyperintense lesion anteriorly measuring 4 x 3 cm, likely
reflecting a complex cyst, although incompletely evaluated on this
non-contrast study.  A 1.2 x 1.2-cm simple cyst is seen posteriorly within the
spleen. Both adrenal glands are unremarkable in appearance.  Both native
kidneys have been surgically removed.  Very limited images of the upper pole
of the transplant kidney are obtained (3:19).  

No upper abdominal lymphadenopathy.  The visualized osseous structures are
unremarkable except to note some degenerative endplate changes throughout the
lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:

1.  1.3-cm CBD has increased very gradually in size from 1 cm in ___.  This
tapers abruptly at the level of the ampulla.  Ampullary stenosis cannot be
excluded; however, given the slow interval progression and similear appearance
morphologically on the prior study as well, this is unlikely to be clinically
significant.

2.  Gallstones and adenomyomatosis in the gallbladder without evidence of
cholecystitis.

3.  Numerous hepatic cysts including one large complex cyst likely with prior
hemorrhage.

4.  1.9-cm pancreatic cyst.

5.  Heterogeneous T2-hyperintense lesion within the spleen, likely a complex
cyst.

6.  The native kidneys have been removed and the transplant kidney is
incompletely evaluated on this study.

The pertinent findings were dicussed with Dr. ___ by telephone at
1.30pm.
